text:
The week closed with the Nifty 50 up 2.61% to 25,800.6 and the Bank Nifty rallying 5.90% to 64,635.2, while the India VIX rose 11.74% to 17.32, signalling higher volatility. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers for the 17th straight session, adding INR 32,647 crore, whereas Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold INR 12,698 crore for the third consecutive session. Breadth was healthy, with a score of 69.9, 72% of stocks above their 20‑day average and 20 new 52‑week highs versus only two lows, indicating broad participation across sectors.

In IPO news, Mahanadi Coalfields Limited opened its OFS on 19 Nov and will close on 23 Nov with a price band of ₹129‑₹136; total subscription was 0.48 times the offer, led by QIBs at 1.37 times. Recent listings performed well: BLS Polymers Limited opened at ₹150 and closed 81% above issue price, while SFC Environmental Technologies rose 34% since listing. No new IPOs are scheduled for the coming week.

Looking ahead, the market may react to several catalysts: a possible shift in Brent crude (now $88.58, down 7.58%) and gold (now $3,573.3, down 8.05%) prices, the USD‑INR at 92.66 (down 1.46%), and global equity weakness (S&P 500 down 5.56%). Domestic drivers include continued FII buying, DII selling pressure, and sector momentum—banks and financials remain in the leading quadrant, while oil & gas and healthcare stay lagging. These factors could shape index direction in the next trading session.
